pr_semantic_analysis.change_summary: Databricks connections now use a dedicated execution context that discovers and tracks the server's current catalog, can seed an empty bootstrap catalog setting, and copies a default catalog into derived contexts. Catalog-selection failures are logged and suppressed rather than propagated.

behavior_changes.description: New Databricks execution contexts use the Databricks-specific implementation; an independently initialized context refreshes defaults, including querying the database for its current catalog.
evidence: The execution-context factory now returns DatabricksExecutionContext.
Initialization without a source context calls refreshDefaults with bootstrap settings enabled.

behavior_changes.description: When the current-catalog query returns a nonempty name, the context tracks that catalog and, when bootstrap settings are in use, fills an otherwise empty bootstrap default-catalog name. Default-catalog lookup then resolves the tracked name through the data source.
evidence: A nonempty query result updates activeCatalogName when it differs.
An empty bootstrap default is populated from the query result.
getDefaultCatalog resolves a nonempty activeCatalogName through the data source.

behavior_changes.description: A context initialized from another Databricks context attempts to select the source context's default catalog rather than independently refreshing the server defaults.
evidence: The source context's default catalog is read and, when non-null, applied to the new context.

behavior_changes.description: If the inherited catalog-selection operation throws DBCException, callers of the Databricks override no longer receive that failure; it is recorded only as a debug log, and the tracked catalog name is updated only after a successful superclass call.
evidence: The superclass catalog-selection call and state update are inside a try block whose DBCException handler only logs.

important_symbols.reason: Controls whether a context discovers defaults from the database or inherits a catalog from another context, and assumes both contexts are DatabricksExecutionContext instances.
Routes newly created Databricks contexts to the new catalog-aware implementation.
Introduces the database query, active-catalog synchronization, bootstrap-setting mutation, and failure-handling behavior.
Defines catalog-switch state synchronization and suppresses catalog-selection exceptions.
Changes the catalog reported to callers when a server-derived or explicitly selected active catalog name is present.

investigation_hints.description: Trace execution-context construction and initialization, including cloned, metadata, and auxiliary contexts, to verify the Databricks-specific type and source-context assumptions.

Trace consumers of default-catalog state and bootstrap settings to determine whether the discovered catalog affects navigation, SQL qualification, reconnect behavior, or persisted connection settings.
Inspect catalog-switch callers and framework contracts to determine whether suppressing DBCException can leave callers believing a catalog change succeeded.

local_risks.description: A failed catalog switch is suppressed, so a caller can continue after requesting a new catalog while the underlying connection and activeCatalogName remain on the previous catalog. If callers rely on the declared throwing contract to prevent further work, subsequent operations could target an unintended catalog.

local_risks.description: When activeCatalogName is nonempty, default-catalog lookup returns the data-source lookup result directly. If metadata has not loaded or cannot resolve that server-reported name, callers may receive null rather than the superclass default fallback.

affected_boundaries.label: Databricks execution-context creation and catalog initialization
evidence: The createExecutionContext source returns new DatabricksExecutionContext(instance, type), and the established call edge records createExecutionContext -> DatabricksExecutionContext at DatabricksDataSource.java:97.
The initializeContextState source casts the supplied context to DatabricksExecutionContext and invokes refreshDefaults when initFrom is null.
Established call edges record initializeContextState -> getDefaultCatalog, initializeContextState -> refreshDefaults, and initializeContextState -> setDefaultCatalog at DatabricksDataSource.java:81.

The refreshDefaults source opens a JDBC metadata session and executes a current-catalog query, while setDefaultCatalog delegates to the superclass and updates activeCatalogName only after successful completion.
affected_boundaries.reason: The Databricks data-source lifecycle crosses into the specialized execution-context service to construct a context and initialize or inherit its active catalog state.
affected_boundaries.uncertainty: The callers and lifecycle paths entering createExecutionContext and initializeContextState are not supplied, and alternate context-construction paths or non-Databricks values reaching the casts are not established.
